zh: 边长为 s 的正方形放得下，当且仅当存在连续 s 栋楼且它们的高度都至少为 s；而且如果 s 放得下，更小的边长也一定放得下。
可行性随边长单调，所以对边长 s 二分；每次用一遍线性扫描检查“高度 ≥ s 的连续楼数能否达到 s”。
二分范围是 [0, min(n, 最大高度)]；check(s) 维护当前连续满足高度 ≥ s 的楼数 run，不满足就清零，run ≥ s 时返回可行（s=0 总是可行）；取最大的可行 s，输出 s×s（用 64 位整数）。
en: A square of side s fits if and only if some s consecutive buildings all have height at least s; and if side s fits, every smaller side fits too.
Feasibility is monotone in the side, so binary search on s; each check is one linear scan asking whether a run of buildings with height >= s reaches length s.

Search s in [0, min(n, maximum height)]; check(s) keeps run, the number of consecutive buildings with height >= s, resetting it on a shorter building, and succeeds once run >= s (s = 0 always succeeds); take the largest feasible s and print s * s using 64-bit integers.

explanationEn:
## Approach

Test whether a side length s is feasible: scan the heights and check whether there are at least s consecutive buildings whose heights are all at least s. Feasibility can only stay the same or become false as s grows, so binary search for the largest s; the answer is s².

## Correctness

A group of consecutive buildings all at least s tall can hold a square of width s and height s; conversely, any square of side s must cover at least s consecutive buildings, all of height at least s. So the check is equivalent to feasibility, and the monotone binary search finds the largest side.

## Complexity

The binary search takes O(n log(min(n,max(h)))) time and O(1) extra space.
